name: Question 12
problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14096572/assets/0cdaa9545b4e0688d23868f876187653ad01b95f59348d9b9121af9a55563380.png)

The region $R$ is enclosed inside the sphere ${x}^{2}+{y}^{2}+{z}^{2}=14z$ for $x\le 0,$ shown above. 
Express the following triple integral in spherical polar coordinates. 

$$
{∭}_{R}z\,\text{d}V
$$
worked_solution:
We will use the change of variables formula in the form

$$
{∭}_{R}f(x,y,z)\,dV={∭}_{Δ}\,f(\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\rho \operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ)\,{\rho }^{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ\,d\rho \,d\theta \,dϕ.
$$

If $(\rho ,\theta ,ϕ)$ are the spherical coordinates of a point, then its Cartesian coordinates $(x,y,z)$ can be found by using the following formulas:

$$
x=\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\,y=\rho \operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\,z=\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ
$$

Notice that the region $R$  represents one-half of the sphere of radius $7$ centered at $(0,0,7).$

With that in mind, let's now write the ${x}^{2}+{y}^{2}+{z}^{2}=14z$ in spherical polar coordinates:

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}+{z}^{2} & =14z \\ {\rho }^{2} & =14\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ \\ \rho (\rho -14\operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ) & =0\end{aligned}
$$

 

Since $\rho $ cannot be identical to zero on the entire sphere, we must have $\rho =14\operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ.$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14096572/assets/1d7643c7855d4de05e02036eb3ca452592d5feea6c09e4b37c2b84fbe4b440b5.png)

 

As a result, we obtain that in spherical polar coordinates, our region can be expressed as 

$$
Δ={(\rho ,\theta ,ϕ)\,:\,0\le \rho \le 14\operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ,\,\frac{\pi }{2}\le \theta \le \frac{3\pi }{2},\,0\le ϕ\le \frac{\pi }{2}}.
$$

Next, we substitute the spherical polar coordinates into the function $f(x,y,z)=z:$

$$
\begin{aligned}f(x,y,z) & =f(\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\rho \operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ) \\  & =\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, using the change of variables formula, we obtain  

$$
\begin{aligned}{∭}_{R}z\,\text{d}V & ={∭}_{Δ}\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ\cdot {\rho }^{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ\,d\rho \,d\theta \,dϕ \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}{\int }_{\pi /2}^{3\pi /2}{\int }_{0}^{14\operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ}{\rho }^{3}\operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ\operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ\,d\rho \,d\theta \,dϕ.\end{aligned}
$$

Question 12
?

The region R is enclosed inside the sphere x2+y2+z2=14z for x≤0, shown above. Express the following triple integral in spherical polar coordinates. ∭RzdV

a
∫0π/2∫π/23π/2∫014cos⁡ϕρ3cos⁡ϕsin⁡ϕdρdθdϕ
b
 ∫0π/2∫π/23π/2∫014cos⁡ϕρ2sin⁡ϕdρdθdϕ
c
 ∫0π/2∫π/23π/2∫014cos⁡ϕρ3cos⁡ϕdρdθdϕ
d
 ∫0π∫π/23π/2∫07cos⁡ϕρ3cos⁡ϕsin⁡ϕdρdθdϕ
e
 ∫0π∫π/23π/2∫07cos⁡ϕρ2cos⁡ϕdρdθdϕ
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

We will use the change of variables formula in the form

∭Rf(x,y,z)dV=∭Δf(ρcos⁡θsin⁡ϕ,ρsin⁡θsin⁡ϕ,ρcos⁡ϕ)ρ2sin⁡ϕdρdθdϕ.

If (ρ,θ,ϕ) are the spherical coordinates of a point, then its Cartesian coordinates (x,y,z) can be found by using the following formulas:

x=ρcos⁡θsin⁡ϕ,y=ρsin⁡θsin⁡ϕ,z=ρcos⁡ϕ
